title: Declare benchmark environment contract and CI validators for regression-proofing
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our benchmarks and load tests produce noisy or inconsistent tokens/sec and p95 latency numbers across CI runs because of drift in GPU driver versions, CUDA runtime, and unpinned base images used by different runners. This makes regression detection unreliable and increases time spent triaging false positives.

Goal: Define a platform-level 'benchmark environment contract' (BEC) describing exact supported OS images, driver/CUDA combinations, pinned runtime container images, and runner configuration. Implement CI validators that enforce the BEC in our benchmark CI, and add regression detection rules that ignore runs that do not meet the contract.

Scope: benchmark CI and perf harnesses for tokens/sec and p95 tracking; standardize pinned images on both PR and nightly pipelines; create lightweight validators for runner capabilities (GPU brand, driver, CUDA toolkit, kernel modules, NUMA topology, CPU governor); update dashboards to only include contract-compliant runs for regression alerts.
acceptance_criteria: A published BEC doc (Confluence link) enumerating supported driver/CUDA pairs, base images with checksums, and runner labels
CI validator job that fails when benchmark runner does not match the BEC (checks driver version, CUDA library SONAMEs, image digest)
Benchmark ingestion pipeline filters out non-compliant runs from regression scoring and p95/tokens/sec baselines
Nightly canary matrix covering at least 3 driver/CUDA combos (e.g., Nvidia 535 + CUDA 12.2, Nvidia 530 + CUDA 11.8, Ampere-optimized image) with pinned image digests
Dashboard alerts only fire on contract-compliant regressions; historical cleanup script tags legacy runs with reason codes
A migration plan and rollback steps for teams that need temporary exemptions (documented SLA and contact)
Automated test in CI proving validator catches an intentionally mismatched driver version

2026-03-05 - Mei Zhang (SRE): Suggest adding a non-blocking mode for early rollout to avoid breaking nightly runs for teams not yet migrated. We'll surface failures as warnings for one week before enforcement.
